question: In self-attention, where do the queries, keys and values come from?
options: Queries from the decoder, keys and values from the encoder
All three are linear projections of the same input sequence
Keys and values are fixed random vectors
Queries are the labels
explanation: Self-attention relates a sequence to itself: Q = X W_q, K = X W_k, V = X W_v.

question: For a sequence of n tokens, what is the shape of the attention weight matrix (per head, per example)?
options: n x n
n x d
d x d
1 x n
explanation: Every query is scored against every key, giving one n x n matrix whose rows sum to 1.

question: Why are attention scores divided by sqrt(d_k)?
options: To make the weights sum to 1
To reduce memory usage
Because dot products of unit-variance vectors have variance d_k; scaling keeps scores near unit scale so the softmax does not saturate
To make attention causal
explanation: In the lesson, std(q.k) was exactly sqrt(d). Unscaled, the softmax became nearly one-hot for large d.

question: How does a causal mask prevent position t from attending to later positions?
options: It sets the values of later positions to zero
It removes later tokens from the input
It multiplies the attention weights by 0.5
It sets their scores to -inf before the softmax, so their weights become exactly 0
explanation: exp(-inf) = 0, so masked positions get zero weight and the remaining weights still sum to 1.

question: You shuffle the tokens of a sequence and run a self-attention layer (no positional information). What happens to the output?
options: It is shuffled in the same way and otherwise unchanged
It stays in the original order
It becomes random
It becomes all zeros
explanation: Self-attention is permutation equivariant: it has no notion of position until you add one.

question: Why could the per-token MLP not solve the counting task, while one attention layer could?
options: The MLP had fewer parameters
Counting needs information from other positions, and only attention moves information between tokens
The MLP used ReLU instead of softmax
The attention model was trained longer
explanation: A per-token MLP sees one token at a time. The count depends on the whole sequence, which attention aggregates.
